title: Certified Information Computation for Cumulative-Incidence Contrasts under Mixed Censoring
banked_reason: D0.5 math and decision PASS; all nine sources verified-attested. Incremental score ceiling 5.2 below field 7.4; independent MAIN validity confirms no bounded faithful same-topic field repair. Bank downgraded under standing mill decision.
gap_reasons: The delivered information and inference results are a narrow marked specialization of the inverse-information framework in van der Laan (1998) and the scalar timing theory in Li–Li (2025), rather than a new identification framework.

The computational addition certifies nearly linear accuracy dependence for fixed histograms, while its matching power comes from mandatory uncompressed step-output size and establishes neither optimal variance computation nor useful work bounds for growing fitted pilots.

The projected score is limited by this narrow contribution and by the absence of a general implementation or finite-sample evidence connecting the certificates to usable inference beyond the selected-law calculation.

D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery completed two solver rounds and a whole-paper maximality audit. It produced an internally audited deterministic prefix-antiderivative Richardson algorithm for fixed finite-description designs and positive rational histogram inputs, with centered step timing scores, full continuous residual certificates, fitted-law variance enclosures, and fixed-input work O(epsilon_num^-1[1+log(epsilon_num^-1)]^8). It also proves an Omega(epsilon_num^-1) lower bound for explicit uncompressed step-table output on one legal fixed input, while explicitly leaving variance-only, compressed/higher-order, unrestricted method-optimal, and growing-pilot total-sample complexity unresolved. The decision and mathematical D0.5 reviews pass with no findings, all nine cited leaves are verified-attested, and the maximality audit finds no further strengthening available from the discharged arguments. Formalization was never entered because the result failed the field novelty floor at D0.5.
tldr: A known mixed-censoring design admits certified computation for a randomized cause-1 cumulative-incidence contrast. On fixed finite-description inputs, a prefix-antiderivative Richardson procedure returns centered step timing scores, full continuous residual certificates and fitted-law variance enclosures with work \(O(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{num}}^{-1}[1+\log(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{num}}^{-1})]^8)\). A legal uniform-inspection input requires \(\Omega(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{num}}^{-1})\) work to deliver an uncompressed step table, matching this accuracy power up to logarithms. The existing information and one-step inference results separate timing gains from an irreducible cause-mark term. The new work result is a partial computational sharpness result on fitted inputs, not unrestricted numerical optimality. General CAR and Li--Li timing theory are credited; PLCO motivates a prospective ascertainment design.
gap: General censored-mixture variance algorithms and all-cause timing grids do not supply the targeted combination of finite encoding, endpoint and atom bookkeeping, outward continuous residual computation, numerical work and constructed marked-score delivery. A supplied residual certificate alone does not establish executable inference.
fill: Cellwise inverse regularity supplies a first-order step-sieve rate. Validated interval arithmetic propagates atom, endpoint, centering, matrix and survivor errors into full residuals and variance enclosures under a stated bit model. The \(n^{-1}\) procedure delivers the budgets for efficient causal inference; sharp certified work is an open question.
